entities.name: PMID:25423535
observations: Male Sprague-Dawley rats received a 32%-kcal-fat diet for 4–6 weeks, producing obesity-prone and obesity-resistant phenotypes; controls received 10%-kcal fat. Trauma was Grade V splenic injury with 30 minutes of hypotension at MAP 30–40 mmHg.
In obesity-prone rats, shock did not produce the prolonged R/K times, reduced alpha angle, or reduced coagulation index seen in controls and obesity-resistant rats; MA decreased in all groups.

The study supports prevention of the acute traumatic coagulopathy phenotype in obesity-prone rats, but it is a small preclinical animal study and the abstract reports directionality rather than numerical effect sizes.

entities.name: Obesity prevents traumatic coagulopathy
observations: In a rat trauma/hemorrhagic-shock model, diet-induced obesity prevented most shock-associated hypocoagulable thromboelastography changes in obesity-prone animals; controls and obesity-resistant animals developed acute traumatic coagulopathy.
This finding is phenotype-specific and does not establish that obesity prevents acute traumatic coagulopathy in humans.

entities.name: Gonadorelin
observations: Pulsatile GnRH administration can induce gonadotropin secretion and ovulation in hypothalamic infertility.
Continuous GnRH or GnRH-agonist exposure suppresses pituitary gonadotropins after an initial flare.

entities.name: PMID:3920942
observations: 1985 review discussing therapeutic applications of luteinizing-hormone-releasing hormone and its analogs.

entities.name: Hypothalamic amenorrhea
observations: Pulsatile GnRH replacement is used to restore gonadotropin secretion and induce ovulation in selected patients with hypothalamic dysfunction.

entities.name: Prostate cancer
observations: Continuous GnRH-agonist treatment suppresses testosterone after pituitary desensitization and is an established endocrine therapy.
